title: rTMS for Incontinence After Prostate Treatment
official: Non-invasive Brain Neuromodulation in Men for Management of Incontinence After Prostate Treatment: a Proof-of-concept Study
summary: Incontinence after prostate treatment (IPT) affects up to 25% of men following radical prostatectomy or other prostate therapies, primarily resulting from sphincteric weakness and impaired neuromuscular control. Current management options, including behavioral therapy and surgical implants, are often limited by modest effectiveness or invasiveness. Emerging neuroimaging evidence demonstrates that the pelvic supplementary motor area (pSMA) in the brain plays a critical regulatory role in controlling pelvic floor muscles and urethral sphincter activity. This proof-of-concept, prospective, randomized clinical trial aims to evaluate the safety, tolerability, acceptability, and procedural feasibility of targeting the pSMA using non-invasive repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in adult males with IPT, alongside a cohort of continent controls. A total of 23 participants will be enrolled (targeting 10 evaluable IPT subjects and 10 continent controls). Participants undergo baseline fMRI using a natural bladder filling protocol, and a randomized, single-session neuronavigated rTMS protocol with concurrent pelvic floor electromyography (EMG) and functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) to evaluate physiological and neurofunctional changes. Safety and adverse events are monitored closely through a 1-month virtual follow-up visit. Findings from this study will establish foundational evidence for cortical modulation of pelvic floor control in IPT. Additionally, these results will guide the design of a future larger, clinical trial to optimize rTMS parameters and integrate brain neuromodulation into post-prostate treatment rehabilitation strategies.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria (IPT Cohort):

* Adult males (biological sex at birth), aged 22 to 80 years.
* History of prostate treatment (e.g., radical prostatectomy, TURP, HoLEP, Aquablation, water vapor therapy, photoselective vaporization) ≥ 6 months prior.
* Answers "yes" to any sub-item of Question 6 on the ICIQ-UI SF ("When does urine leak?", such as leaks before reaching the toilet, cough/sneeze, during sleep, physical activity, post-void dribbling, or no obvious reason).
* Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score \> 10.
* Eligible per MRI safety screening questionnaire.

Inclusion Criteria (Continent Control):

* Adult males (biological sex at birth), aged 22 to 80 years.
* History of prostate treatment ≥ 6 months prior.
* Selects only "never - urine does not leak" on Question 6 of the ICIQ-UI SF and has a total score = 0.
* Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score \> 10.
* Eligible per MRI safety screening questionnaire.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Answers "never" to Question 6 of the ICIQ-UI SF (for IPT cohort) or answers "yes" to any sub-item (for continent cohort).
* Contraindications to MRI.
* Contraindications to rTMS (personal or immediate family history of seizure disorder, implanted electronic devices or conductive objects in or near the head).
* Active urinary tract infection (UTI) at screening (eligible after adequate treatment).
* Intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA injection within the past 6 months.
* Active use of sacral neurostimulator (SNS) or posterior tibial nerve stimulation (TNS) (history allowed if last stimulation was \> 3 months prior).
* Clinically diagnosed neurological disorders (e.g., Multiple Sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, cerebral aneurysm, hydrocephalus, spinal cord injury with motor/sensory deficits, or advanced dementia defined by MoCA \> 10).
* Parenchymal brain lesions and hemorrhagic stroke within the last 12 months. Taking medications that lower seizure threshold (e.g., bupropion) or heavy alcohol use.
* Diagnosis of interstitial cystitis, history of pelvic radiation, or bladder augmentation.
* Post-void residual (PVR) \> 250 cc.
* Incarcerated individuals.
